_comment: CAPABILITY suite for the MySQL CDC stream source with initial_load, over every table of the employeescdc model -- one table per way a row is identified: accounts (a primary key every update CHANGES: the before-image must carry the old key, the row the new), ledger (a composite primary key), devices (no primary key, a unique index), readings (no primary key and no index) -- and its xp_sentinel (functions/caps_mysqlcdc_initial_load.py::mysqlcdc_initial_load). The same stages as postgrescdc_initial_load: (1) domains -- create the mysqlcdc domain, install the employeescdc model, load the xs seed, its operations appended to ${XP_WORK_DIR}/ops.jsonl (--emit-ops) -- as every data command below appends its own; (2) actions, tagged live -- `sentinel-data --key after-create-data`, so the snapshot carries it; (3) collections; (4) functions -- register the @stream_publisher, which STARTS it: with initial_load=True it first emits a snapshot of each tracked table (rows as inserts, a LOAD control row per table ahead of them), then captures changes over the binlog, from the GTID position the snapshot's brief global read lock pinned (server_id 812 for this suite, 813 for the other, so both run at once); (5) sentinel -- hold until after-create-data is in xp_sentinel_changes (the load has flushed); (6) actions, tagged live -- one `modify-data --ops Mix --sets 5` pass, then `sentinel-data --key after-changes`; (7) sentinel -- hold until after-changes has arrived; (8) actions, tagged check -- scripts/verify_cdc_ops.py checks every <table>_changes against ops.jsonl: the snapshot the state the seed left, the changes after it the operations modify-data applied, one by one, in the same transactions, each with its whole before-image and the whole row it leaves; (9) monitor. mysqlcdc_initial_load_live is the same with changes running throughout the snapshot. Run: `tdd xp one-shot --suite container-connectors/mysqlcdc_initial_load --keep`. verify-ops runs with --cascades unlogged --noops unlogged: the binlog has no row event for what a cascade takes (InnoDB applies it below the binlog) nor for a row an UPDATE did not change, so none may arrive.
